source.original_question: In the figure above, if the angle (not shown) where lines n and p intersect is twice as large as the angle (also not shown) where lines l and m intersect, what is the value of x?

audit.source_question: In the figure above, if the angle (not shown) where lines n and p intersect is twice as large as the angle (also not shown) where lines l and m intersect, what is the value of x?
audit.current_question: In the figure above, if the smaller angle (not shown) where lines n and p intersect is twice as large as the smaller angle (also not shown) where lines l and m intersect, what is the value of x?
audit.adaptation_reason: Specified smaller angles for the two unshown line intersections to remove the source acute/obtuse ambiguity; retained the drawn orientation and all numeric conditions.
audit.independent_solution: l is perpendicular to p. The smaller angle between m andp is70, so the smaller angle between l andm is20. The stipulated n–p angle is40; therefore x=90−40=50 degrees.
